rubric.evidence: Every load-bearing claim traced to a primary source fetched live 2026-11-01: css-navigation-1 §2.2 (matching rule quoted verbatim; trigger element kinds a/area/form/input-submit/button) and §4 (navigation state struct, phases, pre-reveal null source element, fully-active requirement), runtime_enabled_features.json5 (NavigationSourcePseudoClass status stable, implied_by RouteMatching), ChromeStatus API record 6327898878377984 (desktop/Android/WebView 156, vendor views, finch name), BCD css/selectors/navigation-source.json (chrome 156, firefox/safari false, experimental true), webstatus.dev absence (empty search + id 404), csswg-drafts #11801 (origin, :navigation-trigger → :nav-source → :navigation-source history, closed completed via PR #14122 on 2026-07-01), intent-to-ship thread (2026-09-03, three LGTMs).

Feature id 6327898878377984 confirmed in the milestone=156 listing under 'Enabled by default' (fetched 2026-11-01); slug css-pseudo-class-for-navigation-source-element derived from the exact listing name 'CSS pseudo-class for navigation source element' per invariant #1. Trunk flag state is stable (not experimental), so the eyebrow carries 'enabled by default' and no warn-block is required; the baseline banner still states Limited availability honestly.

The developer-facing surface is a single argument-less pseudo-class; it is documented on the overview with all nine dimensions (syntax+specificity+feature-detect, matchable elements, effects, invalid-selector degradation, context, navigation-state lifecycle, examples, BCD compat, security/privacy). reference-contract.json claims implementation-sufficient with 1 inventory item and 13 sources. The wider css-navigation-1 surface (@location, @navigation, navigation()) is explicitly out of scope and linked in see-also; those are separate chromestatus features.

The lifecycle section explains the non-obvious parts a developer must know: matching happens in the OUTGOING document only, the destination document reconstructs state with source element null, script navigations have no source element, pre-reveal navigations never reflect in CSS, and a second navigation moves the match.

The spec's own two examples are quoted (thumbnail view-transition-name; form/submit outline) plus feature-detection and :where() isolation patterns. Examples are source-derived; not executed against a local Chrome 156 (environment Chrome predates 156), disclosed here rather than implied.

Real per-version BCD table (Chrome 156, Chrome Android/WebView 156, Edge mirror 156, Firefox false, Safari false) with the BCD file linked; webstatus.dev absence stated with the exact queries; graceful-degradation section covers the invalid-selector-list hazard with the two safe authoring patterns and cites selectors-4 §3.9.

Every cited source is a direct link; all non-GitHub URLs curl-verified 200 on 2026-11-01; GitHub URLs (which reject this environment's HEAD/GET probes with 403) verified via WebFetch content reads (issue #11801 title/state/dates confirmed). Zero unlinked source labels; external links use target=_blank rel=noopener.

Single h1, sequential h2 outline, th scope=row on glance table, thead on data tables, role=note + aria-label on the baseline banner, iframe title, figcaption, and keyboard-scrollable table wrappers (tabindex=0 role=region aria-label per modern-web-guidance responsive-table). guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data table without horizontal overflow on mobile reference page
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Semantic table with thead/th scope; scrollable wrapper with tabindex="0" and role="region" plus an accessible name so keyboard users can scroll; keep header/data relationships intact on small screens.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: every doc-table sits in the house .table-wrap scroller, now with tabindex="0" role="region" and aria-label on each wrapper; headers use th scope/thead; cells wrap via the corpus-wide overflow-wrap default, verified 0px horizontal overflow at 360px.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Treat third-party embeds as untrusted: sandbox them and avoid leaking the embedding page's URL cross-origin.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied via the repo's gendn-kjq posture: sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin" (withholding top-navigation/popups/forms/downloads/pointer-lock) + referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" + loading="lazy" on the showcase iframe.

guidanceConsulted.query: embedding third party iframe lazy loading performance
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Defer offscreen/heavy embeds so they don't compete with initial render.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: the showcase iframe is loading="lazy" and sits below the examples fold; no other third-party content loads on the page.

openQuestions: css-navigation-1 is an early Editor's Draft with open issues on naming and HTML integration (the traversing-navigate-event concept); the matching rule or phase names could change before a Working Draft — the lifecycle section would need re-anchoring.

The spec's Privacy and Security Considerations sections are placeholders ('To be written'); when written, the security-and-privacy section's gendn-derived analysis must be replaced with the normative text.

Whether the submit-button-vs-form source element choice matches Chromium's shipped behavior for every submission path (implicit submission, requestSubmit with/without a submitter) is spec-ambiguous at this draft stage and not asserted on the page.
